title: LECTURE 00 — How to Use This Note
text: LECTURE 00 How to Use This Note এই নোটের উদ্দেশ্য: পরীক্ষায় দ্রুত recall + technically correct answer + sketch-driven presentation Exam Strategy প্রতি Section-এ ৪ সেট থেকে ৩ সেট উত্তর করতে হবে। তাই Section A-তে “সবকিছু অল্প” না পড়ে ৩টি শক্ত set + ১টি backup set প্রস্তুত করো। এই নোটে Very High / High priority প্রশ্নগুলো সেই উদ্দেশ্যে সাজানো হয়েছে। Answer-writing pattern (10-20 marks) 1. Definition / core concept - 2 to 3 lines. 2. Key factors / mechanism - bullets or a compact table. 3. Necessary sketch - labelled and relevant, not decorative. 4. title: LECTURE 02 — Climate & Built Environment: Ancient Wisdom,
text: LECTURE 02 Climate & Built Environment: Ancient Wisdom, Vitruvius and KHANA Historical ideas interpreted as climate-responsive design principles 1. Why climate-responsive design is not a new movement Ancient settlements already used orientation, slope, courtyards, wind protection, solar access and vegetation. The central idea is timeless: a building should respond to the local environment instead of fighting it entirely with mechanical systems. Aristotle and Xenophon  Aristotle: healthy cities benefit from east-inclined slopes and protection from harsh north winds.  Xenophon: south-facing arrangements admit winter sun while high summer sun can be shaded by the roof/portico. Vitruvius - 8 recurring climate-design concerns No. Concern Design meaning 1 Site Choose healthy site conditions. Plan space for appropriate environmental 2 Internal space response. Select material according to natural 3 Nature vs material conditions. 4 Construction vs health Construction should protect health. 5 Comfort vs temperament Design for human comfort response. 6 Sustainability Use resources rationally. Plan streets/buildings with sun and wind in 7 City planning mind. Movement and environmental connection 8 Connectivity affect comfort. PagePage

title: LECTURE 03 — Climatic Comfort & Human Heat Exchange
text: LECTURE 03 Climatic Comfort & Human Heat Exchange Section A-এর সবচেয়ে repeated theory cluster 1. Factors of climatic comfort Factor What it changes Bangla cue Air temperature Sensible heat gain/loss by convection. বাতাস কত গরম/ঠান্ডা Radiation / surrounding surface Radiant exchange with sun, walls, roof, temperature hot/cold objects. চারপাশের surface heat Humidity Controls evaporation potential. ঘাম শুকাবে কি না Air movement Changes convection and evaporation. বাতাস চলাচল Memory T-R-H-A = Temperature - Radiation - Humidity - Airflow. মনে রাখো: “তাপ-রশ্মি-আর্দ্র তা-বাতাস”. 2. Human thermal comfort The human body continuously produces heat through metabolism. Thermal comfort requires a steady thermal state in which surplus heat is dissipated without excessive physiological strain. Core mechanisms: conduction, convection, radiation and evaporation. Heat-balance equation - exam-safe form M-W=C+R+K+E+S PagePage

title: Lecture example: approx. 45% radiation, 30% — Calm warm air + moderate RH Radiation + convection + evaporation
text: M = metabolic heat; W = useful mechanical work; C = convection; R = radiation; K = conduction; E = evaporation; S = body heat storage. At steady state, S approx. 0. সহজ ভাষায়: শরীর যত net heat তৈরি করে, প্রায় ততটাই পরিবেশে ছাড়তে পারলে body temperature steady থাকে। জমে গেলে S positive -> শরীর গরম হয়; বেশি হারালে S negative -> শরীর ঠান্ডা হয়। 3. Deep body / skin temperature and physiological response Core body temperature is maintained close to 37 C. The lecture material treats skin temperature as roughly 31-34 C in hot-condition heat-exchange discussion. Vasomotor adjustment changes skin blood flow to regulate heat transfer. Condition Key idea Design relevance Vasoconstriction reduces skin blood flow; Cold Reduce drafts; conserve heat. shivering may increase metabolic heat. Vasodilation increases skin blood flow; Provide air movement and evaporation Warm/hot sweating supports evaporative cooling. opportunity. Evaporation becomes ineffective; body Dangerous: maximize ventilation, reduce Hot + saturated + still air heat may accumulate. radiant load. 4. Heat loss in four climatic situations Situation Dominant process Exam point Lecture example: approx. 45% radiation, 30% Calm warm air + moderate RH Radiation + convection + evaporation convection, 25% evaporation. Convection/radiation loss decreases as Evaporation becomes increasingly important Hot air + considerable radiation air/surface temperatures approach skin if air is dry enough. temperature. Moving air removes saturated film around Hot air + radiation + air movement Air movement is a key relief mechanism. skin and accelerates evaporation. Air warmer than skin + saturated + still Very little sensible or evaporative heat loss. Heat-stroke risk; potentially fatal conditions. Correction note Higher air speed increases evaporation and usually improves evaporative cooling when the air is not saturated. It does not automatically increase ambient relative humidity ; the key exam idea is “moving air removes the saturated boundary layer at the skin”. MATCHING QUESTION BANK [VERY HIGH PRIORITY] Q. title: LECTURE 05 — Comfort Indices, Cosine Law, Atmospheric
text: LECTURE 05 Comfort Indices, Cosine Law, Atmospheric Depletion, Humidity & Air Movement Definitions, differences and short-note answers 1. Subject variables affecting comfort Comfort is not determined by climate alone. Clothing, acclimatization, age and sex, body shape/fat, health, food/drink and other personal factors modify thermal sensation. 2. ET, CET, EW and Operative Temperature Index Combines Core exam definition / limitation Equivalent sensation scale; originally based ET - Effective Temperature Air temperature + humidity + air movement on equal-comfort lines. Radiation is not directly included. ET corrected to account for radiant CET - Corrected Effective Temperature ET variables + radiation effect environment; widely used in the course material. Air temp + humidity + mean radiant temp + Can underestimate cooling effect of air EW - Equivalent Warmth skin/clothing surface response movement at high humidity. Useful where humidity and air movement OT - Operative Temperature Air temperature + mean radiant temperature effects are small/negligible. Memory ET = 3 variables; CET = ET + radiation. OT = Air + Radiation. EW = “whole warmth response” including body/clothing surface measurements. 3. Cosine Law Page Page

title: Angle of incidence is measured from the surface normal.
text: Angle of incidence is measured from the surface normal. I_tilted = I_normal x cos(beta) beta = angle between the incident ray and the normal to the surface. More oblique incidence -> lower intensity per unit area. 4. Atmospheric depletion Solar radiation is reduced while passing through the atmosphere by absorption and scattering due to ozone, water vapour, dust, clouds and other particles. A longer atmospheric path generally means greater depletion. সহজ ভাষায়: সূর্যের রশ্মি atmosphere-এর ভিতর যত বেশি পথ যায়, তত বেশি অংশ absorb/scatter হয়। তাই low sun angle-এর radiation বেশি depleted হতে পারে। 5. Unsaturated air Contains less vapour than saturation capacity. Evaporation is possible. Contains more vapour than equilibrium Supersaturated air Unstable; condensation tends to occur. saturation capacity. Actual water vapour amount per unit Absolute Humidity (AH) Used in RH calculation with matching units. mass/volume (as defined in course material). AH / saturation humidity at same Relative Humidity (RH) Dimensionless percentage. temperature x 100%. RH = (AH / SH) x 100% AH and SH must be expressed on a consistent basis at the relevant temperature. 6. title: LECTURE 07 — Design Specifications: Layout, Spacing, Air
text: LECTURE 07 Design Specifications: Layout, Spacing, Air Movement & Enclosure The design-answer chapter: always draw 1. Design specification checklist The lecture organizes climate-responsive design around five practical controls: Layout, Spacing, Air movement, Enclosure and Shading Device. Shortcut L-S-A-E-S = Layout - Spacing - Air movement - Enclosure - Shading. মনে রাখো: “লেআউট-স্পেস-বাতাস- খোলস-ছায়া”. 2. Layout for wind and climate  Broad spacing can improve breeze penetration in warm-humid climates.  Staggered layout often avoids wind shadows and improves airflow through a group of buildings.  Building orientation can be adjusted about 30-45 degrees to wind direction where suitable to improve exposure and flow distribution.  In hot-dry/composite cases, compactness may reduce exposed surface area and unwanted heat gain; design must respond to season and climate type. 3. Spacing and functional distribution  Organize functions according to heat, privacy, day/night use and air movement.  Use floor height and internal voids/courtyards to support air movement and thermal stratification.  Separate served and service zones where this helps buffer unwanted heat. P/A ratio For a given floor area, a compact form generally has a lower perimeter-to-area (P/A) ratio, which reduces exposed envelope area. Circular/compact geometries have low P/A ratios, while highly articulated forms have higher exposure. 4. Air movement and openings Page Page

title: Cross ventilation - a high-value exam sketch.
text: Cross ventilation - a high-value exam sketch. Opening decision Effect Determines pressure difference and airflow path through Position occupied zone. Size Controls flow area; too-small openings restrict ventilation. Control / louvers Can direct air upward/downward and regulate rain/privacy. Cross ventilation Requires connected inlet-outlet path across the space. 5. Enclosure  Material and thermal capacity determine heat storage and time lag.  Degree of enclosure balances protection against the need for airflow.  Insulation, roof build-up and external surface reflectance can reduce heat entry. 6. Warm-humid vs hot-dry design Warm-humid Hot-dry Maximum ventilation with large openings. Control hot dusty wind; selective ventilation. Maximum shading of direct and diffuse radiation. Compactness / shaded external spaces often beneficial. Avoid heat storage where possible. Use thermal mass and time lag strategically. Reflective surfaces, ventilated double roof. Courtyard / evaporative cooling can help where water is available. Protect against glare and long-wave re-radiation from surrounding Vegetation should shade but not block useful breeze. hardscape. title: LECTURE 09 — Shading Devices & Effective Shading
text: LECTURE 09 Shading Devices & Effective Shading Solar control with orientation-sensitive sketches 1. Why shading? The principal purpose of sun shading is to prevent unwanted solar radiation when external conditions are above comfort level. Shading can also help control glare, rain exposure, privacy/visibility and sometimes wind direction. Solar path into building Meaning Direct radiation Beam radiation directly through an opening. Reflected radiation Solar radiation reflected from ground/adjacent surfaces. Scattered sky radiation, important in cloudy/warm-humid Diffuse radiation conditions. Solar heat absorbed by roof/wall and later conducted/radiated Indirect through opaque surface inward. 2. External vs internal shading External shading is generally more effective for heat control because it stops solar radiation before it passes through the glazing and becomes indoor heat. Internal curtains can control glare but the absorbed solar heat is already inside the envelope. 3. Types Basic types: horizontal, vertical and combined shading. Type Best suited conceptually for Examples High-angle sun; often useful on south-facing Horizontal exposures in many northern-hemisphere Overhang, canopy, horizontal louvers. situations. Page Page

title: 3. Rat-trap bond
text: 3. Rat-trap bond Rat-trap bond places bricks on edge so that a cavity is created within the wall thickness. The lecture emphasizes reduced material use, lower cost and improved thermal/sound insulation when correctly detailed. Rat-trap bond conceptual plan / cavity sketch. Construction rule Why it matters Use consistent, good-quality bricks Bond geometry depends on dimensional consistency. Bottom and top courses solid Stability and closure of cavity. Sill/lintel and opening jamb zones solid Allows frame fixing and local strength. Reinforcement at corners/openings where designed Improves integrity / earthquake detailing. Plan services through cavity carefully Improves finish but must not weaken wall. Correction note The slide states wall strength is “not compromised”. Exam-safe wording: properly designed and constructed rat-trap masonry can provide adequate wall performance, but structural capacity depends on brick quality, workmanship, detailing and applicable code requirements. 4. Green vs Sustainable building Green building Sustainable building Focuses on measurable reductions in water, energy, waste and indoor Broader life-cycle goal balancing environment, society and economy. environmental impacts. Can be “greener than baseline” without solving every life-cycle issue. Requires long-term viability and wider system thinking. Typical actions: efficient energy/water, resource conservation, Includes resilience, affordability, social equity, durability and healthier indoor spaces. environmental performance. title: LECTURE 11 — Non-thermal Microclimate: Ventilation, Air Space,
text: LECTURE 11 Non-thermal Microclimate: Ventilation, Air Space, Infiltration & Numericals Formula-based preparation - do not leave this chapter for the exam hall 1. Objectives of ventilation / air change  Supply adequate oxygen for breathing and other purposes.  Remove carbon dioxide.  Remove unwanted heat and moisture.  Reduce staleness and smell / pollutants. 2. How ventilation rate is expressed Core numerical relationship. ACH = (Q x 3600) / V Q in m3/s; V = room volume in m3. If Q is in L/s, first divide Q by 1000. Air space per person = (net room volume) / number of users Net room volume may subtract major furniture/occupant volume if the problem specifically requires it. 3. Recommended air space and fresh-air supply (course table) Air space/person (m3) Minimum (L/s/person) Smoking zone Non-smoking zone 3 11.3 22.6 17.0 6 7.1 14.2 10.7 Page Page

9 5.2 10.4 7.8 12 4.0 8.0 6.0 Table-reading rule প্রথমে room volume / person থেকে air-space category নির্ধারণ করবে; তারপর smoking/non- smoking condition দেখে L/s/person নেবে; শেষে total Q = rate x number of persons. 4. Relative humidity numerical RH = (AH / SH) x 100% Example: AH = 12 g/m3, SH = 17 g/m3 -> RH = 70.6%. 5. Ventilation numerical - worked example Example: room 45 m x 23 m x 3 m, 200 persons, non-smoking. Volume V = 3105 m3, so air space/person = 15.525 m3. Using the highest listed 12 m3 category, the course table gives 6.0 L/s/person for a non-smoking zone. 11. Required fresh air = 200 x 6.0 = 1200 L/s = 1.20 m3/s. 12. ACH = 1.20 x 3600 / 3105 = 1.39 air changes/hour (approx.). Exam caution If the teacher expects interpolation or a different table-selection convention, follow the convention demonstrated in class. The uploaded table itself ends at 12 m3/person. 6. Heat loss due to air change Heat loss rate = rho x Q x c_p x (T_inside - T_outside) Standard engineering form. If ACH is given: Q = ACH x V / 3600. rho is air density, c_p is specific heat. Standard engineering note যদি question-এ air density না দেওয়া থাকে, engineering calculations often use about 1.2 kg/m3 near room conditions. এটি slide table-এর অংশ নয়; exam-এ teacher/class convention অনুসরণ করবে। 7. Fire shelter / laboratory safety logic 13. Calculate total room volume. 14. Calculate air space per person. 15. From the course table, find required fresh air per person for the occupancy condition. 16. Compare required total fresh air with available supply. 17. If inadequate, improve by increasing fresh-air supply, increasing volume, reducing occupancy, or improving the ventilation arrangement. MATCHING QUESTION BANK [VERY HIGH PRIORITY] Q. Define Absolute Humidity (AH) and Saturation Point Humidity (SH) and calculate Relative Humidity (RH) from given vapour densities. Page Page

Common mistakes to avoid  Do not write ET and CET as the same thing - CET includes radiation effect.  Do not measure solar incidence angle from the surface itself in the cosine law; use the angle from the surface normal.  Do not claim air movement always cools by lowering air temperature - it improves convection/evaporation and changes perceived comfort.  Do not use KHANA rules as universal modern codes - state the Bengal/Bangladesh climatic context.  Do not draw shading devices without showing sun direction / blocked ray.  In ventilation numericals, convert L/s to m3/s before using ACH formula.  Always state units. title: LECTURE 01 — Climatic Study & Bioclimatic Architecture
text: LECTURE 01 — Climatic Study & Bioclimatic Architecture 1. Climatic Design কেন দরকার? Climatic design হলো এমন design approach যেখানে building-কে স্থানীয় climate-এর সাথে “fit” করানো হয়, যাতে comfort পাওয়া যায় এবং mechanical energy demand কমে। Lecture slide-এর মূল কথা: “Building must be designed to fit in with their climate.” Climatic study কী সাহায্য করে Design implication Comfortable indoor climate temperature, airflow, solar exposure নিয়ন্ত্রণ Energy-saving structural design passive control আগে; mechanical system পরে Protection from external factors sun, wind, rain, humidity অনুযায়ী envelope Natural resource utilisation sunlight, breeze, vegetation, site features ব্যবহার Regional architectural character ভিন্ন climate → ভিন্ন form, opening, material, method Shortcut / মনে রাখার কৌশল — C-E-P-N Comfort → Energy saving → Protection → Natural resources. Climatic study-এর benefits এই ৪ শব্দে মনে রাখো। Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে নিচের wording পাঠযোগ্য করার জন্য সামান্য normalised করা হয়েছে; বছর ও marks স্ক্যানে যতটা স্পষ্ট, ততটাই রাখা হয়েছে। Year Marks Matching question / focus 2016 10 Importance of climate study for a BECM graduate. 2017 15 Where can a BECM professional use learning from Climate & Architectural Design? 2. কেন building form এক জায়গা থেকে আরেক জায়গায় বদলায়?  Climate condition building arrangement/design-কে প্রভাবিত করে।  Requirement determination (কী পরিমাণ shade/ventilation/thermal protection দরকার) climate নির্ভ র।  Equipment selection climate-load-এর সাথে সম্পর্কি ত।  Building method, material এবং formation regional climate-এর প্রতিক্রিয়া। Core idea Same function ≠ same building. Climate বদলালে form, envelope, opening, roof, material এবং orientation বদলাতে পারে। 3. Bioclimatic Architecture Bioclimatic বলতে lecture slide-এ “relationship between living organisms and architecture” বোঝানো হয়েছে। অর্থাৎ nature/environment-এর logic ব্যবহার করে building form ও performance optimize করা।  Nature-inspired response, কিন্তু শুধুই aesthetic imitation নয়।  Sun, wind, terrain, vegetation ও seasonal conditionকে design input হিসেবে নেয়।  Goal: comfort + lower energy demand + better environmental fit. Source-note Introduction slide ecological consideration-কে syllabus-এর অংশ হিসেবে দেখায়; তবে এই slide set-এ ecological consideration-এর আলাদা detailed lecture নেই। তাই এখানে unsupported detail যোগ করা হয়নি।

title: LECTURE 02 — Global Climatic Factors
text: LECTURE 02 — Global Climatic Factors 1. Climate vs Weather Term Meaning Time scale Climate একটি স্থানের দীর্ঘ সময়ের weather প্রায় 20-30 years pattern Weather নির্দি ষ্ট সময় ও স্থানের atmospheric day-to-day / short term condition Shortcut / মনে রাখার কৌশল — Weather = Today, Climate = Trend আজ কী হচ্ছে = weather; দীর্ঘমেয়াদে সাধারণত কী হয় = climate। 2. Latitude, Altitude & Land-Water Relationship  Latitude = Equator-এর উত্তর/দক্ষিণে angular distance. Low latitude বেশি solar exposure পায়; high latitude তু লনামূলক ঠান্ডা।  Altitude = mean sea level-এর ওপরে উচ্চতা. Lecture slide: air rises becomes cooler; তাই পাহাড়ের ওপর নিচের তু লনায় ঠান্ডা।  Large water body climate moderate করে, কারণ land-এর তু লনায় water ধীরে heat up/cool down করে।  Tropical environment roughly 23.5°N থেকে 23.5°S; lecture slide-এ rainforest, monsoon, savanna climate উল্লেখ করা হয়েছে। Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে নিচের wording পাঠযোগ্য করার জন্য সামান্য normalised করা হয়েছে; বছর ও marks স্ক্যানে যতটা স্পষ্ট, ততটাই রাখা হয়েছে। Year Marks Matching question / focus 2018 15 Why is it always colder at higher altitudes? Discuss with examples. 2024 12 Why is there a large day-night temperature difference in hot desert / subtropical regions? 3. Eleven Global Climatic Factors — master list No. Factor 1 Solar radiation quality 2 Solar radiation quantity 3 Tilt of the Earth's axis 4 Radiation at the Earth's surface 5 Earth's thermal balance 6 Winds: thermal forces 7 Trade winds: Coriolis force 8 Mid-latitude westerlies 9 Polar wind 10 Annual wind shifts 11 Influence of topography Shortcut / মনে রাখার কৌশল — 1-5 = Sun/Earth, 6-10 = Wind, 11 = Topography Global factorsকে তিন ব্লকে ভাঙো: (1-5) solar/earth processes, (6-10) circulation/winds, (11) topographic modification.

title: Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে
text: Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে নিচের wording পাঠযোগ্য করার জন্য সামান্য normalised করা হয়েছে; বছর ও marks স্ক্যানে যতটা স্পষ্ট, ততটাই রাখা হয়েছে। Year Marks Matching question / focus 2016 25 Analyze major factors of global climate variations in different geographic locations. 2024 - Multiple questions from tilt, ITCZ, wind pattern and radiation at earth surface. 4. Solar Radiation Quality  Earth প্রায় সব energy সূর্য থেকে পায়; solar radiation climate-এর dominant influence.  Spectrum in lecture: 290-2300 nm.  UV: 290-380 nm photochemical effects, sunburn etc.  Visible: 380-700 nm.  Short infrared: 700-2300 nm radiant heat dominant.  Shorter wavelengths-এর কিছু অংশ atmosphere absorb করে। 5. Solar Radiation Quantity  Course slide solar constant = 1395 W/m² at upper atmosphere.  Sun output-এর জন্য প্রায় ±2% variation; Earth-Sun distance change-এর জন্য ±3.5% variation.  Aphelion ≈ 152 million km; perihelion ≈ 147 million km (lecture value). Exam-safe line Quality = wavelength / type of solar energy; Quantity = intensity / amount of solar energy. 6. Earth-Sun Relationship & Tilt of Earth's Axis Sketch: Earth-Sun relationship, solstices and equinoxes  Earth axis orbital plane-এর সাথে lecture slide অনুযায়ী 66.5°; equivalent tilt from the perpendicular is about 23.5°.  Maximum solar intensity-এর zone Tropic of Cancer (around 21 June) ও Tropic of Capricorn (around 21 December)-এর মধ্যে migrate করে.  Around 21 March and 23 September, sun’s rays equator-এ প্রায় normal equinox condition.

title: 7. Radiation at the Earth's Surface
text: 7. Radiation at the Earth's Surface Surface-এ পৌঁছানো radiation তিনটি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ কারণে বদলায়: angle of incidence, atmospheric depletion এবং sunshine duration. 7.1 Cosine Law If radiation is oblique, same energy spreads over a larger area; intensity falls. I_tilted = I_normal × cos β β = angle between solar ray and the normal to the surface  Normal incidence energy concentrated intensity maximum.  Oblique incidence → same radiation larger area-তে spread intensity কম। 7.2 Atmospheric Depletion Atmosphere-এর ozone, vapour, dust ইত্যাদি radiation absorb/scatter করে; ফলে surface-এ energy কমে। 7.3 Duration of Sunshine Daylight/sunshine কতক্ষণ পাওয়া যাচ্ছে সেটি total solar receipt-কে প্রভাবিত করে। Duration আর intensity একই জিনিস নয়—এই distinction পরে Elements of Climate-এ আবার আসবে। Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে নিচের wording পাঠযোগ্য করার জন্য সামান্য normalised করা হয়েছে; বছর ও marks স্ক্যানে যতটা স্পষ্ট, ততটাই রাখা হয়েছে। Year Marks Matching question / focus 2023 10 Evaluate Radiation of the Earth's Surface from global climate variation viewpoint. 2024 9 Evaluate Radiation of the Earth's Surface from viewpoint of climate variation at global scale.

title: Lecture balance: 50% of incoming solar energy reaches the ground (23% diffuse + 27% direct), and the ground returns 50% — through long-wave radiation + evaporation + convection. This balance prevents indefinite heating.
text: 8. Earth's Thermal Balance Redrawn from lecture: incoming and outgoing percentage balance Incoming component Course value Reflected from ground 5% Reflected from cloud 20% Absorbed in atmosphere 25% Diffuse radiation reaching ground 23% Direct radiation reaching ground 27% Outgoing from ground Course value Long-wave radiation 20% Evaporation, then radiation 20% Convection, then radiation 10% Total 50% Core logic Lecture balance: 50% of incoming solar energy reaches the ground (23% diffuse + 27% direct), and the ground returns 50% through long-wave radiation + evaporation + convection. This balance prevents indefinite heating. title: 9. Global Wind Pattern — mechanism
text: 9. Global Wind Pattern — mechanism Pressure belts and prevailing surface winds  Equator বেশি heat পায় → surface air warm, expands, becomes light rises equatorial low pressure.  Rising warm-humid air upper level-এ subtropical zone-এর দিকে যায়; cooling/densification-এর পর ~30° latitude- এ sink করে → subtropical high.  Subtropical high থেকে এক branch equator-এ ফেরে (trade wind), অন্য branch subpolar front-এর দিকে যায় (westerlies).  Polar region cold/dense polar high; surface flow subpolar low-এর দিকে → polar easterlies.  এভাবে Hadley, Ferrel, Polar circulation cells ও pressure belts তৈরি হয়। Shortcut / মনে রাখার কৌশল — 0-30-60-90 0° = low (ITCZ), 30° = high, 60° = low, 90° = high. Pressure-belt sequence মনে রাখলে wind pattern সহজ হয়। 10. Thermal Force & Coriolis Force Force What it does Exam phrase Thermal force Unequal heating থেকে pressure Motive force of wind. difference ও convective circulation তৈরি করে. Coriolis force Earth rotation moving air-এর direction Modifies wind direction. deflect করে. Result Thermal + Coriolis → trade winds / Both are needed to explain actual wind global wind pattern. direction. Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে

ITCZ, Doldrums & Annual Wind Shift  At equator, northern and southern trade winds meet and air rises Inter -Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ ).  Surface wind may be calm/light and irregular sailors call it “Doldrums ”.  ITCZ maximum solar heating zone-কে follow করে; July-এ northward, January-এ southward shift.  Annual shift temperature, wind direction এবং rainfall-এর seasonal change ঘটায়. Conceptual seasonal migration of ITCZ Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে নিচের wording পাঠযোগ্য করার জন্য সামান্য normalised করা হয়েছে; বছর ও marks স্ক্যানে যতটা স্পষ্ট, ততটাই রাখা হয়েছে। Year Marks Matching question / focus 2016 15 Assess impact of annual wind shift from north to south of equator. 2021 10 Describe relationship between ITCZ and annual wind shifts with figures. 2023 10 Define doldrums and explain its location and formation. 2024 12 Why is ITCZ generally calm, and why does it shift more toward the Northern Hemisphere? 12. Mid-latitude Westerlies, Polar Winds & Topography  Westerlies: subtropical high থেকে subpolar low-এর দিকে surface flow; Coriolis deflection gives westerly character.  Polar easterlies: polar high থেকে subpolar low-এর দিকে cold surface air; Coriolis deflection gives easterly flow.  Topography regional pressure/temperature/wind patternকে modify করে; land, forest, water differentially heat হয় এবং mountains wind path বদলায়.

title: LECTURE 03 — Elements of Climate & Climatic Data
text: LECTURE 03 — Elements of Climate & Climatic Data 1. Elements that matter to a building designer Element Why it matters to design Temperature heat gain/loss, comfort, material response Humidity & vapour pressure evaporation, condensation, comfort, decay Precipitation & driving rain roof/drainage/envelope leakage risk Solar radiation heat gain, daylight, shading Wind ventilation, heat loss, pressure/rain exposure Sky condition diffuse radiation/daylight Vegetation shade, wind filtering, surface moisture/evaporation Shortcut / মনে রাখার কৌশল — T-H-P-S-W-S-V Temperature, Humidity, Precipitation, Solar, Wind, Sky, Vegetation — 7 elements. 2. Climatic Information: raw data → design data Meteorological station-এর raw data directly designer-এর answer নয়। Building designer-কে beneficial/harmful features identify করার জন্য data analyse করতে হয়। Design logic Record → Analyse → Identify extremes/means → Translate into design requirement. 3. Temperature Measurement  Unit: °C; mercury thermometer commonly used in slide.  Continuous record: thermograph.  True air temperature shade-এ measured; thermometer louvered wooden Stevenson screen-এর ভিতরে রাখা হয়.  Height: about 1.20-1.80 m above ground (lecture slide).  Useful data: daily max/min + diurnal range; monthly mean/extremes; annual mean/extremes/range. title: Year Marks Matching question / focus
text: Year Marks Matching question / focus 2021 5 Short note: Stevenson Screen. 2022 10 Which instrument is required to measure temperature in open field? Show working mechanism of Stevenson Screen. 4. Humidity — AH, RH & Vapour Pressure Term Definition / formula Unit Absolute Humidity (AH) Actual moisture present per unit g/kg or g/m³ mass/volume of air. Relative Humidity (RH) Actual moisture / moisture-holding % capacity at same temperature × 100 Vapour pressure (Pv) Partial pressure due to water vapour in N/m² air. RH = AH / SH × 100 (%) SH = saturation humidity / moisture-holding capacity at that temperature P = Pa + Pv Atmospheric pressure = partial pressure of dry air + partial vapour pressure  RH measured with wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer; readings can be interpreted using psychrometric chart .  Humidity data can be analysed as daily, monthly and annual maxima/minima/means. Bangla intuition AH বলে “আসলে কত জলীয়বাষ্প আছে”; RH বলে “এ তাপমাত্রায় যতটা ধরতে পারত, তার কত শতাংশ ভরা আছে।” 5. Precipitation  Rain, hail, dew, snow, frost—atmosphere থেকে deposited water-এর collective term.  Measured by rain gauge; unit commonly mm/day or mm/month.  Monthly pattern dry/wet season দেখায়.  Maximum 24-hour rainfall flooding risk-এর guide; maximum hourly rainfall intensity surface drainage design- এর জন্য প্রয়োজন. title: LECTURE 03.1 — Elements for Building Designers
text: LECTURE 03.1 — Elements for Building Designers 1. Driving Rain & Driving Rain Index (DRI) Driving rain = wind-driven rain যা verticalভাবে না পড়ে angle-এ building envelope-এ আঘাত করে এবং joints, window reveals, cracks/gaps দিয়ে water penetration ঘটাতে পারে। Driving rain mechanism and DRI thresholds DRI = Annual Rainfall (m) × Annual Average Wind Speed (m/s) Unit in the lecture: m²/s Exposure DRI Design meaning Sheltered m 3² / s Low combined wind-rain exposure; normal detailing Moderate 3-7 m²/s More careful joints, sills, reveals and weatherproofing Severe > 7 m²/s Highly exposed/coastal/hilltop; robust envelope and gap control Worked example from slide Annual rainfall 1.2 m × average wind 4.0 m/s = DRI 4.8 m²/s → Moderate exposure. Shortcut / মনে রাখার কৌশল — R × V DRI মনে রাখো: Rainfall × Velocity. বেশি rain বা বেশি wind—দুটিই exposure বাড়ায়। Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে নিচের wording পাঠযোগ্য করার জন্য সামান্য normalised করা হয়েছে; বছর ও marks স্ক্যানে যতটা স্পষ্ট, ততটাই রাখা হয়েছে। Year Marks Matching question / focus 2021 5 Short note: Driving Rain. 2022 10 Define driving rain. Explain how to design exposure of a building using DRI.

title: Year Marks Matching question / focus
text: Year Marks Matching question / focus 2023 10 Define driving rain. Explain building exposure design using driving rain index. 2024 7 Define driving rain. Write in detail how to design exposure of a building using DRI. 2. Sky Condition & Cloud Cover  Sky condition mainly cloud presence/absence দিয়ে described হয়.  Typical observation around 09:00 and 15:00; night records comparatively limited.  Cloud cover tenths/eighths (octas) বা percentage-এ expressed হতে পারে: 50% = 5/10 = 4/8.  Designer-এর observation time/frequency জানা দরকার, কারণ sky condition diffuse radiation ও daylight influence করে. 3. Solar Radiation — Sunshine Duration vs Radiation Intensity Item Sunshine Duration Radiation Intensity Meaning How long bright sun shines Actual radiant power per unit area Typical unit hours/day, monthly average W/m²; also Btu/ft²·h, kcal/m²·h Instrument Sunshine recorder (Campbell-Stokes type) Pyranometer / pyrheliometer / actinometer / solarimeter Design use Long-term sunshine availability Directly relates to solar heat gain Very important distinction Zero bright-sunshine hours does NOT mean zero solar energy: an overcast sky can still deliver diffuse radiation. 4. Wind Measurement  Wind velocity: cup-type / propeller anemometer.  Wind direction: wind vane.  Continuous velocity + direction record: anemograph.  Free wind: open flat country at ~10 m height; urban reading ~10-20 m to reduce obstruction effects.  Unit: m/s; other units may include ft/min, mph, knot.

title: 5. Wind Rose — how to read
text: 5. Wind Rose — how to read Longer spoke = wind occurs more frequently from that direction  Direction: spoke যে দিক দেখায়, wind সেই direction থেকে এসেছে.  Frequency: spoke length / radial scale দ্বারা বোঝা যায়.  Speed classes: colour/segment দ্বারা বিভিন্ন speed range দেখানো যায়.  “Calm” percentage center-এ separately দেওয়া হতে পারে. title: LECTURE 04 — Classification of Tropical Climate
text: LECTURE 04 — Classification of Tropical Climate 1. Basis of classification  Lecture credits G. A. Atkinson (1953).  Basis: extremes of temperature and humidity affecting human comfort.  Tropical climates are divided into three major zones plus three sub-groups (six named types in the slide ). Major / subgroup types Warm-humid equatorial climate Warm-humid island or trade-wind climate Hot-dry desert or semi-desert climate Hot-dry maritime desert climate Composite or monsoon climate Tropical upland climate Shortcut / মনে রাখার কৌশল — 3 pairs Warm-humid (equatorial + island) | Hot-dry (desert + maritime) | Seasonal (composite + upland). Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে নিচের wording পাঠযোগ্য করার জন্য সামান্য normalised করা হয়েছে; বছর ও marks স্ক্যানে যতটা স্পষ্ট, ততটাই রাখা হয়েছে। Year Marks Matching question / focus 2021 10 Explain salient features affecting classification of tropical climates as suggested by G. A. Atkinson. 2023 10 Write classification of tropical climate and explain how climate zones are formed on earth. 2. Warm-Humid Equatorial Climate Parameter Lecture profile Location roughly within ~15° N and S Air temperature Mean max 27-32°C; mean min 21-27°C; narrow diurnal/annual range RH ~75%, may vary ~55-100% Vapour pressure ~2500-3000 N/m² Rainfall ~2000-5000 mm/year; severe short storm may ~100 mm/h Sky Cloudy ~60-90%; glare possible Solar radiation Partly reflected/scattered by clouds; diffuse component important Wind Generally low, but strong squalls possible Vegetation / ground Rapid growth, high water table/waterlogging possible Special risks Mould, algae, rust, rot, insects Shortcut / মনে রাখার কৌশল — গরম-ভেজা-মেঘ-বৃষ্টি Warm-humid = high humidity + heavy rain + cloudy sky + small temperature range. “দিন-রাত খুব বেশি বদলায় না।” Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে নিচের wording পাঠযোগ্য করার জন্য সামান্য normalised করা হয়েছে; বছর ও marks স্ক্যানে যতটা স্পষ্ট, ততটাই রাখা হয়েছে। Year Marks Matching question / focus 2016 20 Compare characteristics of Hot-dry and

title: Year Marks Matching question / focus
text: Year Marks Matching question / focus Warm-humid climate. 2023 10 Describe features of warm-humid equatorial climate with examples. 2024 16 Why is climate warm and humid between equator and about 15° N/S? Explain using climatic features. 3. Hot-Dry Desert / Semi-Desert Climate Parameter Lecture profile Location approximately 15-30° N and S Hot-season day max 43-49°C Hot-season night min 24-32°C Cold-season night min 10-18°C Diurnal range Very high: ~17-22°C RH Low: ~10-55% Rainfall Very low/variable: ~50-155 mm/year; long dry periods possible Sky Mostly clear; dust haze may create glare Solar radiation Strong/direct by day; strong night re-radiation under clear sky Wind Hot, local, dusty; dust storms possible Vegetation Sparse; dry soil; low water table Material issue Rapid day-night temperature swing may crack materials Shortcut / মনে রাখার কৌশল — দিন আগুন—রাত ঠান্ডা Hot-dry-এর exam identity: very hot day + cooler night + low RH + clear sky + strong direct sun + little rain + dust. Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে নিচের wording পাঠযোগ্য করার জন্য সামান্য normalised করা হয়েছে; বছর ও marks স্ক্যানে যতটা স্পষ্ট, ততটাই রাখা হয়েছে। Year Marks Matching question / focus 2016 20 Compare Hot-dry with Warm-humid climate. 2022 15 Describe features of composite/monsoon and hot-dry desert climatic patterns with examples. 2024 12 How does hot desert form in subtropical region and why is day-night temperature range large? 4. Composite / Monsoon Climate  Large land masses near tropics; marked seasonal changes in solar radiation and wind direction .  Usually two dominant seasons; lecture says roughly two-thirds hot-dry and one-third warm-humid; sometimes cool-dry third season.  Examples on slide: Lahore, Mandalay, Asuncion, Kano, New Delhi. Season Day mean max °C Night mean min °C Diurnal range °C Hot-dry 32-43 21-27 11-22 Warm-humid 27-32 24-27 3-6 Cool-dry Up to 27 4-10 11-22  Dry period RH ~20-55%; wet season RH ~55-95%.  Monsoon rain intense/prolonged; annual rainfall lecture range ~500-1300 mm.  Sky: overcast/dull in monsoon; clear/dark blue in dry season.  Wind: dry season hot/dusty; monsoon wind fairly strong and steady.  Seasonal humidity change may weaken materials; dust/sand storms may occur.

title: LECTURE 05 — Regional, Site & Urban Climate
text: LECTURE 05 — Regional, Site & Urban Climate 1. Macroclimate, Site Climate & Microclimate Regional data is the starting point; local modifiers create site-specific deviation . Scale Meaning Regional / macroclimate Broad climate described by regional/met station data. Site climate Climate of the actual area available for the project, horizontally and vertically. Microclimate Very local climate around a building/space; scale depends on discipline. Important Macroclimate is useful as a guide, but lecture says it is seldom sufficient in accuracy for a particular site. 2. How to assess site climate for a large site 6. Start with regional climatic data. 7. Identify dominant local factors and expected deviations. 8. Use available site observation/measurement where possible. 9. Take advice from experienced local observer/expert if long observation is impossible . 10. Select the area most suitable for habitation / project purpose. title: 3. Factors Constituting Regional Climate
text: 3. Factors Constituting Regional Climate Level Factors Primary Global climatic factors; detailed slide highlights temperature, humidity, air flow as primary climatic outcomes. Secondary Location of region; diurnal variation; altitude. Tertiary Soil condition; topography; natural wind breakers; man-made wind breakers; water bodies; cities/industries; deserts. Local & minor Ocean current; sky condition; smog; smoke; fog; thunder/lightning; sand storms. Shortcut / মনে রাখার কৌশল — P-S-T-L Primary → Secondary → Tertiary → Local. প্রথমে hierarchy লিখলে বড় প্রশ্নের structure নিজে থেকেই তৈরি হয়। 4. Key local modifiers — quick explanations Factor Effect Soil condition Stony/sandy surface quickly heats and reradiates; fine/organic soil behaves differently. Topography Cool heavy air settles in depressions → locally cooler/humid conditions. Natural wind breaker Mountains/large trees obstruct or redirect wind. Ocean current Warm/cool currents transport heat and modify coastal temperature/humidity/rainfall. Smog / smoke / fog Modify humidity, radiation, visibility and air quality. Sand storm Openings/ventilators require protection; façade treatment may respond to dust/sand. Deviation Factors  Air temperature  Temperature inversion  Humidity  Precipitation  Sky condition  Solar radiation  Air movement / wind velocity gradients  Special characteristics  Vegetation Source-note The uploaded site-climate slide lists “temperature inversion” as a deviation factor but does not separately define or derive it. Therefore this note does not invent a detailed mechanism beyond the source. In an exam, identify it as a local/vertical temperature-structure deviation factor unless your teacher has given a fuller class explanation.

title: 6. Urban Climate
text: 6. Urban Climate  Changed surface qualities: pavements/buildings absorb more solar energy ; evaporation decreases .  Buildings cast shadows, block/channel wind, store heat and release it slowly.  Energy seepage: AC/refrigeration, electrical appliances, engines and industry add heat .  Atmospheric pollution forms a barrier to outgoing radiation. Conceptual urban heat-island profile Effect reported in slide Value / behaviour City-countryside temperature deviation up to about 8°C Relative humidity in urban area about 5-10% lower Wind velocity may drop to less than half of adjoining countryside Flow around buildings turbulence / eddies at leeward corners Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে নিচের wording পাঠযোগ্য করার জন্য সামান্য normalised করা হয়েছে; বছর ও marks স্ক্যানে যতটা স্পষ্ট, ততটাই রাখা হয়েছে। Year Marks Matching question / focus 2021 10 Distinguish between urban and macroclimate. 2022 15 Analyze factors responsible for deviation of urban climate and effects of deviation. 2023 15 Analyze factors responsible for deviation of urban climate and its effects. 2024 8 Urban climate depends on human intervention — explain.

title: LECTURE 06 — Thermal Comfort & Human Heat Balance
text: LECTURE 06 — Thermal Comfort & Human Heat Balance 1. Why Thermal Comfort matters  Daily life cycle = activity fatigue recovery ; unfavorable climate এই cycle disturb করতে পারে.  Thermal stress discomfort, reduced efficiency এবং health breakdown ঘটাতে পারে.  Therefore building designer must understand both climate and how the human body acts/reacts to heat . Definition idea Thermal comfort = এমন thermal condition যেখানে মানুষের body heat balance বজায় থাকে এবং ব্যক্তি পরিবেশকে thermally acceptable মনে করে. Lecture emphasis is on physiological balance and comfort variables. Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে নিচের wording পাঠযোগ্য করার জন্য সামান্য normalised করা হয়েছে; বছর ও marks স্ক্যানে যতটা স্পষ্ট, ততটাই রাখা হয়েছে। Year Marks Matching question / focus 2023 10 Describe significance of thermal comfort for human body. 2024 12 What is thermal comfort? How does the human body maintain thermal balance? 2. Metabolism & Heat Production  Metabolism = foodকে living matter ও energy-তে convert করার process.  Basal metabolism = continuous automatic/vegetative process.  Muscular metabolism = consciously controlled muscular work.  Lecture slide states roughly 20% produced heat is used inside body and remaining 80% surplus heat must be dissipated. Activity Heat production (W) — lecture table Sleeping Min. 70 Sitting / typing / light bench work 130-160 Sitting, heavy arm/leg movements 190-230 Standing moderate work / some walking 220-290 Walking + moderate lifting/pushing 290-410 Intermittent heavy lifting/digging 440-580 Hardest sustained work 580-700 Maximum heavy work ~30 min Max. 1100 Source-note Billah Sir class note marks the heat-production table as “not need to memorize”; understand the trend: more activity → higher metabolic heat.

title: 3. Human Heat Gain & Heat Loss
text: 3. Human Heat Gain & Heat Loss Redrawn heat-exchange sketch: conduction, convection, radiation , evaporation Mode Heat gain / loss logic Metabolism Internal heat production. Conduction Direct contact; depends on surface temperature difference. Convection Heat exchange with air touching skin/clothing; faster air movement usually increases convective exchange. Radiation Heat exchange with surrounding surfaces / sun without direct contact. Evaporation Sweat + imperceptible perspiration + breathing; dry air allows faster evaporation. Shortcut / মনে রাখার কৌশল — C-C-R-E Heat-loss routes: Conduction, Convection, Radiation, Evaporation. Body temperature & steady state  Deep body temperature must remain balanced around 37°C.

Human Thermal Balance Equation Met - Evp ± Cnd ± Cnv ± Rad = 0 Metabolism - evaporation ± conduction ± convection ± radiation = thermal steady state Sign idea Conduction / convection / radiation can be gain or loss depending on direction of heat flow, তাই ± sign. Evaporation is written as heat loss in the lecture equation. What happens if the equation is unbalanced? 2023 12 Write thermal balance equation and describe regulatory mechanisms when it is unbalanced. 6. Vasomotor Adjustment, Sweating & Shivering Thermoregulatory response flowchart  If heat balance > 0: skin blood circulation increases skin temperature rises heat -loss processes accelerate (vasodilation-type response).  If heat balance < 0: skin circulation reduces skin temperature falls heat -loss processes slow (vasoconstriction -type response).  If overheating continues despite vasomotor regulation sweating starts.  If underheating continues violent shivering can sharply increase metabolic heat production . Common Exam Traps  Climate এবং weather এক করা যাবে না.  Sunshine duration আর radiation intensity এক জিনিস নয়.  ITCZ “এক জায়গায় fixed” নয়—seasonally shifts.  DRI-তে rainfall ও wind speed দুটোই লাগে.  Warm-humid-এ diurnal temperature range narrow; hot-dry-এ large.  Site climate = regional climate copy নয়; local deviation analyse করতে হয়.  Thermal balance equation-এ Cnd/Cnv/Rad gain বা loss হতে পারে, তাই ±. title: How to Use This Analysis
text: How to Use This Analysis The 3-out-of-4 Reality The safest strategy is not to memorize isolated questions. Each main question often mixes 2-4 subtopics. The eight sets below are preparation clusters built from repeated question families, so mastering one set gives coverage across multiple historical question numbers. FASTEST EXAM STRATEGY Preparation order Set Section A - Priority 1 A1 Thermal Comfort & Heat Exchange Section A - Priority 2 A2 Ventilation & Repeating Numericals Section A - Priority 3 A3 Microclimate / Envelope / Shading Section A - Backup A4 Climate-Context + Climate-Friendly Construction Section B - Priority 1 B1 Global Climatic Factors & Wind System Section B - Priority 2 B3 Regional / Site / Urban Climate Section B - Priority 3 B2 Tropical Climate Section B - Backup B4 Elements / Measurement / Basic Thermal Response Important Warning Do not completely skip the 4th set. From 2021 onward, main questions are highly mixed. If time is short, prepare the first 3 sets deeply and keep a one-page emergency revision sheet for Set 4. DATA SCOPE AND METHOD  Eight regular final-term papers are present in the supplied question bank: 2016, 2017, 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024. A 2019 paper is not present in the uploaded bank.  The 2020 paper is a reduced 120-mark paper with only three main questions per section. It is counted for topic presence, but not treated as a normal four-question structure.  Frequency means a direct question or a close conceptual variant appeared in that paper. It is not a claim that the wording was identical.  Historical papers sometimes place the two teachers' content under different printed section labels. Therefore this analysis maps questions to the CURRENT uploaded Section A / Section B lecture blocks by topic, not blindly by the old printed section heading.  Overlapping topics (especially site climate and thermal comfort) are assigned according to the dominant lecture framing and question style.

title: Question-Type Analysis
text: Question-Type Analysis 1. HIGH-PRIORITY THEORY / DISCUSSION QUESTIONS  A1: Factors of climatic comfort; thermal comfort ideas; human body heat exchange; heat loss in climatic situations; designer responsibilities; comfort indices.  A3: Microclimate design; building-envelope response; spacing and openings; effective shading and seasonal solar control.  A4: Climate-context-comfort; climate vs environment; Khana; Vitruvius; green/sustainable building; tube house; rat- trap bond.  B1: Earth-sun relationship, axial tilt, radiation, earth thermal balance, global wind pattern, ITCZ, Coriolis force, westerlies/polar winds.  B2: Tropical climate classification; warm-humid/hot-dry/composite climates; passive control and climatic design response.  B3: Regional/site/urban climate; factor hierarchy; site-design process; urban climate deviation.  B4: Climatic elements, measurement methods, driving rain, climatic data interpretation and basic thermal response. 2. PROOF / DERIVATION / ANALYTICAL-EQUATION LIST Important The supplied papers contain very few formal mathematical "proofs". What repeatedly appears are equations, relationships, mechanisms and analytical derivations. Prepare the following as derivation-style items.  Thermal balance equation of the human body and interpretation of imbalance.  RH-AH-SH relationship: RH = (AH / SH) x 100%, with numerical use.  Air change / ventilation expressions and heat loss due to air change.  Driving Rain Index: rainfall x annual average wind speed; exposure classification.  Cosine law for incident solar radiation and its building-design applications.  Solar shading geometry: solar altitude/azimuth, horizontal and vertical shadow angles, effective projection and incidence angle.  Earth thermal balance / incoming vs outgoing radiation mechanism.  Heat-transfer logic through conduction, convection, radiation and evaporation. 3. title: 3-Out-of-4 Preparation Strategy
text: 3-Out-of-4 Preparation Strategy If you have enough time Prepare all four sets in each section. This is the only fully safe approach because recent papers deliberately mix subtopics. IF TIME IS LIMITED - SECTION A  1) MASTER A1 completely: theory + diagrams + ET/CET/EW/OT.  2) MASTER A2 numericals: practice at least one air-change, one shelter and one lab problem without notes.  3) MASTER A3 design: envelope + microclimate + shading sketches; practice one solar-shading numerical.  4) BACKUP A4: memorize climate-context-comfort, Khana, tube house, rat-trap bond and sustainability definitions. IF TIME IS LIMITED - SECTION B  1) MASTER B1 completely: earth-sun, radiation, heat balance and world winds.  2) MASTER B3: factor hierarchy + site design + urban climate deviation.  3) MASTER B2: tropical classification + warm-humid vs hot-dry + design response.  4) BACKUP B4: DRI, Stevenson screen, wind graph, climatic measurement and short thermal notes. Last-night rule Do not spend the last night reading entire reference books. Use the set pages in this analysis as the map, then open the matching class slide/note only for diagrams, exact formulas and teacher-specific wording. RECOMMENDED REVISION CYCLE  Day 1: A1 + B1 (highest-recurrence theory).  Day 2: A2 + B3 (numerical + site climate).  Day 3: A3 + B2 (design/sketch + tropical climate).  Day 4: A4 + B4 (backup sets + short notes).  Final revision: numericals, diagrams, comparison tables, then only the S-priority question families.

A1. Climatic Comfort Indices Effective Temperature (ET)  Different air-temperature + humidity combinations can feel equally comfortable.  ET scale combines Temperature + Humidity + Air movement on a psychrometric basis.  Radiation effect is not included in basic ET. Corrected Effective Temperature (CET)  ET scale is corrected by incorporating radiation effect.  Hence CET is more complete than ET where radiant environment matters. Equivalent Warmth (EW) & Operative Temperature (OT)  EW correlates air temperature, humidity, mean radiant temperature with skin/clothing surface temperature.  OT combines effects of radiation and air temperature; humidity and air movement are treated as negligible in the lecture slide. Shortcut - ET-CET ET = T + H + Air movement. CET = ET + Radiation. title: A7. Microclimate & Building Envelope
text: Derivation idea: প্রতি ঘণ্টায় replaced air volume = nV. Mass/hour = ρnV. Heat/hour = mass × cp × ΔT. প্রতি second-এ rate পেতে 3600 দিয়ে ভাগ। Source note Repeated QB numerical gives room volume, air changes/hour, ΔT and specific heat. The uploaded slide does not print the final heat-loss equation; the above is an explicitly marked reconstruction from the heat-energy relation used to solve that question. A7. Microclimate & Building Envelope Roof, wall, floor, opening and other envelope components respond differently to heat, humidity, wind and rain .  Roof: heat enters mainly by conduction after solar heating; time lag and heat conserving capacity matter.  External walls: orientation changes solar exposure; east/west walls receive strong low-angle sun.  Window/opening: admits solar heat, daylight, rain/fog and also acts as infiltration path.  Ventilator/clerestory: higher-level hot-air exhaust can improve ventilation.  Design tools: material, orientation, opening, architectural design, micro-planning, semi-mechanized techniques. title: B4. Global Wind Pattern, Thermal Force, Coriolis & ITCZ
text: B4. Global Wind Pattern, Thermal Force, Coriolis & ITCZ Global pressure/wind belts and circulation cells.  Equator gets intense heating w arm air rises equatorial low pressure.  Subtropical region: cooled upper air sinks high pressure.  Thermal force drives convection from pressure/temperature differences.  Earth rotation modifies motion; Coriolis deflects winds. Trade winds are the resultant of thermal and Coriolis effects.  At equator, N and S trade winds converge: Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), often calm/light irregular breeze = doldrums. ITCZ follows maximum solar heating north-south seasonally . Shortcut - 0-30-60-90 0° Low, 30° High, 60° Low, 90° High - pressure belts মনে রাখার দ্রুত sequence. Cosine Law — derivation 5. ধরা যাক parallel solar beam-এর normal intensity = In এবং surface normal-এর সাথে incidence angle = β. 6. একই beam bundle normal surface-এ projected area B এবং tilted surface-এ larger actual area C-তে ছড়িয়ে পড়ে. 7. Geometry থেকে cos β = B/C, অর্থাৎ B = C cos β. 8. একই total radiation energy হলে intensity ∝ 1/area. তাই tilted surface-এর intensity = In × (B/C). 9. B/C = cos β বসালে Iβ = In cos β. Iβ = In cos β β = 0° ⇒ maximum intensity; β increases ⇒ intensity falls. Directly stated in uploaded source D2. Relative Humidity relation — definition proof 10. AH = given temperature-এ air-এ actual moisture content. 11. SH = same temperature-এ maximum/saturation moisture capacity. 12. Relative humidity মানে actual capacity-এর fraction, expressed as percentage. 13. Fraction = AH/SH. Percentage করতে ×100. RH = (AH / SH) × 100 % All humidity quantities must be expressed on the same mass/volume basis. Directly stated in uploaded source D3. Earth’s Thermal Balance — accounting proof 14. Incoming solar energy = 100% ধরা হয়. 15. 5% ground reflection + 20% cloud reflection + 25% atmosphere absorption = 50% diverted before/around ground heating. 16. Ground receives diffuse 23% + direct 27% = 50%. 17. Ground loses 20% long-wave + 20% evaporation then radiation + 10% convection then radiation = 50%. 18. Therefore ground input = ground output = 50%; long-term thermal balance is maintained in the lecture model . Ground gain = 23% + 27% = 50% = 20% + 20% + 10% = Ground loss

title: Course-slide percentage accounting.
text: Course-slide percentage accounting. Directly stated in uploaded source D4. Human Heat Balance — energy-conservation derivation 19. Metabolism (Met) produces internal body heat. 20. Evaporation (Evp) always removes latent heat, so it is written as a loss term. 21. Conduction (Cnd), convection (Cnv) and radiation (Rad) may be gain or loss depending on environmental temperature gradients; hence ± signs. 22. Steady deep-body temperature means net heat storage = 0. 23. Therefore all gains and losses algebraically sum to zero. Met − Evp ± Cnd ± Cnv ± Rad = 0 If the sum departs from zero, vasomotor adjustment occurs; persistent overheating leads to sweating, underheating to shivering. Directly stated in uploaded source D5. Air Changes per Hour (ACH) — derivation 24. Q = ventilation flow rate in m³/s. 25. One hour = 3600 s, তাই one hour-এ supplied/replaced air volume = 3600Q m³. 26. Room volume = V m³. 27. Number of complete room-volume replacements per hour = supplied volume per hour / room volume. 28. Hence ACH = 3600Q / V. ACH = 3600 Q / V Q in m³/s, V in m³. Derived for solving repeated QB numericals D6. Total Fresh-air Requirement — derivation 29. If each person needs qperson L/s, N persons need N identical shares. 30. Total required supply = sum of individual supplies = N × qperson. 31. Convert L/s to m³/s by dividing by 1000. Qtotal = N qperson ; Q(m³/s) = Q(L/s) / 1000 Use the lecture fresh-air table to choose qperson. Derived for solving repeated QB numericals D7. Heat Loss due to Air Change — derivation 32. Room volume V, air changes n per hour ⇒ air volume replaced per hour = nV. 33. If air density = ρ, mass replaced per hour = ρnV. 34. For temperature difference ΔT, heat carried per hour = mass × cp × ΔT = ρnVcpΔT. 35. Heat-loss rate per second = divide by 3600. 36. Thus Q̇ air = ρVncpΔT / 3600. Q̇ air = ρ V n cp ΔT / 3600 Standard reconstruction for the repeated air-change heat-loss numerical; not printed verbatim in uploaded slide. Derived for solving repeated QB numericals D8. Driving Rain Index — relation, not a mathematical proof DRI = R × Vw R = annual rainfall (m), Vw = annual average wind speed (m/s). Directly stated in uploaded source

title: Conclusion
text: Conclusion A comfortable building does not “cool the body” by one mechanism only; it manages air temperature, surface temperature, humidity and air movement so that the four heat-exchange paths remain physiologically manageable .

title: A1.2 Thermal / Climatic Comfort: factors, ideas and significance
text: A1.2 Thermal / Climatic Comfort: factors, ideas and significance Priority: S - very high | Asked: 2016, 2018, 2023, 2024 | Marks: 5-20 Year Q. Significance of thermal comfort 2023 4(c) 10 for human body. What is thermal comfort? How 2024 3(c) 12 does body maintain thermal balance? Thermal comfort is the condition in which a person feels thermally satisfied and the body can maintain heat balance without excessive physiological effort such as heavy sweating or shivering. Objective climatic variable Effect on comfort Air temperature Controls sensible heat exchange, especially convection. Controls radiant heat gain/loss from roof, walls, sun and other Mean radiant / surrounding surface temperature surfaces. Controls the air’s capacity to accept evaporated moisture ; high RH Humidity reduces sweat evaporation. Changes convective and evaporative heat exchange and therefore Air movement perceived comfort. Subjective / individual variables  Clothing  Acclimatization  Age and sex  Body shape and subcutaneous fat  State of health  Food and drink  Skin colour / individual variation Memory Objective = T-R-H-A: Temperature, Radiation, Humidity, Air movement. Subjective = person-specific variables. Conclusion Thermal comfort matters because sustained thermal imbalance reduces health, concentration and performance; climate - responsive design therefore aims to reduce physiological strain before mechanical conditioning is added.

M-W=C+R+K+E+S For thermal equilibrium, heat produced and gained must equal heat lost. At steady state , S ≈ 0. A positive storage term means body heat is accumulating; a negative storage term means the body is losing stored heat . Imbalance Body response Purpose Vasodilation → more blood to skin; then Too warm / S > 0 Increase sensible and evaporative heat loss. sweating if needed. Vasoconstriction → less blood to skin; Reduce heat loss and increase metabolic Too cold / S < 0 shivering if needed. heat production. Human thermal balance - central equation with regulatory response. Exam line If vasomotor regulation is insufficient in heat, sweating begins; in cold, strong shivering can greatly increase metabolic heat production.

title: A1.9 Vasomotor Adjustment & Autonomic Nervous System
text: A1.9 Vasomotor Adjustment & Autonomic Nervous System Priority: A/S - recent repeat | Asked: 2022, 2023, 2024 | Marks: 6-10 Year Q. Marks Question focus Vasomotor adjustment; autonomic 2022 6(d) 6 nervous system dilate/constrict in ambient temperatures. Vasomotor adjustment in different 2023 5(a) 8 climates. Vasomotor adjustment and design 2024 6(a) 10 implications for comfortable indoor environments. Vasomotor adjustment is the automatic change of blood-vessel diameter, especially near the skin, used by the autonomic nervous system to regulate heat transfer between the body core and the environment. Condition Response Thermal effect More warm blood reaches skin → skin temperature rises → greater Warm / overheating Vasodilation: skin blood vessels widen. convective/radiant loss; sweating may follow. Less warm blood reaches skin → skin Vasoconstriction: skin blood vessels Cold / underheating temperature falls → heat loss slows; narrow. shivering may follow. Vasodilation vs vasoconstriction - redraw as a simple flow diagram. Design implication  Avoid prolonged indoor conditions that force continuous sweating or shivering .  Use air speed to aid evaporation in warm conditions, but avoid excessive cold drafts.  Reduce radiant heat from roofs/walls so vasodilation does not have to compensate for large radiant gains .  Allow adaptive variation rather than a perfectly fixed condition all day.

Data note for 2023 The 2023 paper clearly states a 45×25×3 m room. Workflow: V = L×B×H → air-space/person = V/N → choose the non-smoking rate from the course table → Qtotal = rate×N → convert L/s to m³/s → ACH = Q×3600/V. 2021 solution - 200 persons V = 45×23×3 = 3105 m³. text: A2.4 Fire-shelter safety numericals - complete repeated solution Priority: S - repeated numerical | Asked: 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 | Marks: 8-10 Year Q. Marks Question focus 8×7×3 m shelter, designed 500, 2021 7(a) 10 actual 550, available fresh air 6 L/s. 9×10×3 m shelter, designed 400, 2022 7(d) 10 actual 450, available 6 L/s. 9×10×3 m shelter, 450 occupants, 2023 7(c) 10 available 6 L/s. 8×7×3 m shelter, 550 occupants, 2024 6(d) 8 available 6 L/s. Safety requires both adequate air-space per person and adequate fresh-air flow. The question does not state smoking ; use the “Minimum” column for a basic life-safety check, and mention that a non-smoking comfort target would be more demanding. 2021 / 2024: 8×7×3 m, 550 persons V = 168 m³; air-space/person = 168/550 = 0.305 m³/person This is far below the table minimum of 3 m³/person. Minimum required total fresh air = 550 × 11.3 = 6215 L/s Volume required to provide 3 m³/person = 550 × 3 = 1650 m³ 2022 / 2023: 9×10×3 m, 450 persons V = 270 m³; air-space/person = 270/450 = 0.600 m³/person Minimum required total fresh air = 450 × 11.3 = 5085 L/s Volume required to provide 3 m³/person = 450 × 3 = 1350 m³ Safety verdict Both repeated shelter cases are severely under-provisioned. title: A2.6 Laboratory fresh-air suitability - all repeated variants
text: A2.6 Laboratory fresh-air suitability - all repeated variants Priority: S - repeated numerical | Asked: 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 | Marks: 5 Year Q. Marks Question focus 5×4×2.1 m lab, 20 users, fresh air 5 2021 8(c) 5 L/s; normal + power failure. 2022 8(c) 5 6×5×2.5 m lab, 20 users, 5 L/s. 2023 8(b) 5 6×5×2.5 m lab, 20 users, 5 L/s. 2024 5(d) 5 5×4×2.1 m lab, 20 users, 5 L/s. Case 1: 5×4×2.1 m V = 42 m³; air-space/person = 42/20 = 2.10 m³/person 2.10 m³/person is below the minimum 3 m³/person. Available total fresh air is only 5 L/s = 0.25 L/s/person. At the 3 m³ table row, minimum fresh air would be 11.3 L/s/person (226 L/s total); a non-smoking target is 17 L/s/person (340 L/s total). Therefore the lab is not suitable even with the fan running; during power failure the forced supply becomes zero and the situation is worse. Case 2: 6×5×2.5 m V = 75 m³; air-space/person = 75/20 = 3.75 m³/person Air-space exceeds 3 m³/person, but the fresh-air supply is still only 0.25 L/s/person. Using the conservative 3 m³ bracket, the required flow is at least 226 L/s total (340 L/s for non-smoking). Thus the lab is still unsuitable ; power failure removes the forced supply entirely. Conclusion For both laboratory variants, ventilation capacity - not just room volume - is the decisive failure. Add a properly sized ventilation system, emergency power / passive backup openings and verified outdoor-air paths.

title: A3.3 Cosine Law of Solar Incidence and building applications
text: A3.3 Cosine Law of Solar Incidence and building applications Priority: S - repeated | Asked: 2017, 2021, 2022, 2024 | Marks: 5-10 Year Q. Marks Question focus 2017 7(a-i) part Short note: Cosine Law. Atmospheric depletion and Cosine 2021 6(b) 10 law. Illustrate cosine law; use in 2022 5(c) 5 building design. Describe cosine law and 2024 6(c) 7 applications in climate-responsive built environment. I_surface = I_normal × cos β β is measured between the incident solar ray and the NORMAL to the surface. Cosine law - oblique radiation spreads over a larger surface area. Derivation idea For a beam with cross-sectional area B normal to the rays, the same energy falls on a larger tilted surface area C . Geometry gives B/C = cos β. Since intensity = energy/area, I_C = I_B × (B/C) = I_B cos β. Building applications  Compare solar exposure of roofs and façades at different orientations.  Explain why low-angle incidence gives less energy per unit surface area but creates severe glare and deeper penetration through windows.  Guide orientation and shading design.  Estimate direct-beam component on a tilted surface.

title: A3.4 Atmospheric Depletion and why higher altitude is colder
text: A3.4 Atmospheric Depletion and why higher altitude is colder Priority: A/S - repeated | Asked: 2017, 2021, 2022, 2023 | Marks: 5-10 Year Q. Marks Question focus Short note: Atmospheric 2017 7(a-ii) part Depletion. Atmospheric depletion and Cosine 2021 6(b) 10 law. Atmospheric depletion; why 2022 6(b) 10 colder at higher altitude? 2023 5(c) 5 Illustrate atmospheric depletion. Atmospheric depletion is the reduction of solar radiation as it passes through the atmosphere by absorption and scattering by ozone, water vapour, dust, clouds and other particles. A longer atmospheric path generally causes greater depletion. Incidence and atmospheric path are separate effects on received solar energy. Higher altitude - exam-safe explanation The lecture states that rising air becomes cooler. At lower pressure aloft , ascending air expands and cools , so average air temperature generally decreases with elevation. The atmosphere is also heated strongly from the ground upward , so being closer to the sun is not the controlling effect.

title: A4.3 Rat-trap bond: construction, working and climatic advantages
text: A4.3 Rat-trap bond: construction, working and climatic advantages Priority: S - repeated | Asked: 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023 | Marks: 8-18 Year Q. Marks Question focus Construction technique of brick 2020 2(a) 18 wall using Rat-Trap bond. Working mechanism of rat-trap 2021 7(d) 8 bond. Working mechanism of rat-trap 2022 7(b) 8 bond. Working mechanism of rat-trap 2023 8(c) 8 bond. Rat-trap bond is a brick masonry technique in which bricks are placed on edge/vertical orientation so that a continuous cavity is formed within the wall thickness. The cavity reduces material use and improves thermal and acoustic resistance when the wall is properly detailed. Rat-trap bond - cavity formed within a nominal brick-wall thickness. Construction rules  Use consistent good-quality bricks; dimensional variation affects the bond.  Keep bottom/top closure courses and opening jamb/sill/lintel zones solid where required .  Maintain the cavity without excessive mortar droppings bridging it.  Provide reinforcement/bands/corner detailing where structural design or seismic requirements demand it .  Plan services carefully so the cavity is not unintentionally destroyed. Advantages  Lower brick and mortar use; the lecture slide reports approximately 25% fewer bricks and 40% less mortar than conventional masonry in one comparison.  Cavity improves thermal insulation: cooler inside in summer, warmer in winter.  Lower material demand can reduce cost and embodied impact.  Exposed brickwork can reduce plaster where workmanship is good. Structural caution The slide says strength is not compromised. Exam-safe wording: properly designed and constructed rat-trap masonry can provide adequate wall performance; actual structural capacity depends on materials, workmanship, reinforcement/detailing and code requirements.

Modern urban reinterpretation  Break long depth with courtyards/light wells so internal rooms are not sealed from daylight and air .  Provide low inlet + high outlet to support cross/stack ventilation.  Use shaded semi-outdoor transitional space rather than fully glazed heat-trapping corridors .  Keep privacy through staggered openings/louvers while retaining airflow .  Combine passive airflow with low-energy fans when urban obstruction weakens natural wind.

title: B1.3 Radiation at Earth Surface + Earth Thermal Balance + surface heat
text: B1.3 Radiation at Earth Surface + Earth Thermal Balance + surface heat release Priority: S - highest repeat | Asked: 2016, 2018, 2020, 2021, 2023, 2024 | Marks: 9-15 Year Q. Marks Question focus Earth thermal balance with 2016 2(b) 15 diagram. Ways Earth surface releases heat 2018 5(a) 15 to atmosphere. 2020 6(a) 15 Earth thermal balance. 2021 4(c) 12 Earth thermal balance. Radiation of Earth surface at 2023 2(a) 10 global scale. Radiation of Earth surface and 2024 4(c) 9 global climate variation. Radiation reaching the surface  Angle of incidence / Cosine Law: oblique rays spread the same energy over a larger area.  Atmospheric depletion: ozone, vapour, dust and clouds absorb/scatter radiation.  Duration of sunshine: determines how long solar input can occur. Earth thermal balance - course percentage model. Incoming component Course value Reflected from ground 5% Reflected from cloud 20% Absorbed in atmosphere 25% Diffuse radiation reaching ground 23% Direct radiation reaching ground 27% Outgoing from ground Course value Long-wave radiation 20% Evaporation, then radiation 20% Convection, then radiation 10% Total returned from ground 50% Thus, in the lecture model, 50% of incoming energy reaches the ground (23% diffuse + 27% direct) and the ground returns 50% through long-wave radiation, evaporation and convection. The surface therefore releases heat to the atmosphere mainly in three ways: radiation, latent heat through evaporation, and sensible heat through convection .

title: Coriolis directions
text: Coriolis directions  Northern Hemisphere: moving air deflects to the right.  Southern Hemisphere: moving air deflects to the left.  Therefore trades are easterly, mid-latitude winds are westerly and polar surface winds are easterly.

title: B1.5 ITCZ / Doldrums and Annual Wind Shift
text: B1.5 ITCZ / Doldrums and Annual Wind Shift Priority: S - very high | Asked: 2016, 2021, 2023, 2024 | Marks: 10-15 Year Q. Marks Question focus Impact of annual wind shift from 2016 3(b) 15 north to south of equator. Relationship between ITCZ and 2021 1(b) 10 annual wind shifts. Doldrums: location and 2023 2(b) 10 formation. Why ITCZ is calm and why it shifts 2024 1(b) 12 more toward Northern Hemisphere. Seasonal migration of the ITCZ - conceptual annual shift around the equator. The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is the equatorial/sub-equatorial belt where the NE and SE trade winds converge. Warm moist air rises, so surface horizontal wind can be weak, variable and calm - the traditional “doldrums”. Why it shifts  The zone of maximum solar heating migrates north and south with the apparent seasonal movement of the sun .  ITCZ follows this thermal low, moving northward in northern summer and southward in northern winter .  It often migrates farther north over the Northern Hemisphere because there is more land , and land heats more strongly/quickly than ocean in summer, pulling the thermal low northward. Effects of the annual shift  Seasonal reversal/shift of prevailing winds.  Monsoon circulation and seasonal rainfall migration.  Changes in cloud, humidity and storm activity.  Important seasonal design changes in ventilation and rain protection.

title: B1.6 Earth-Sun Relationship, tilt of axis and seasonal solar distribution
text: B1.6 Earth-Sun Relationship, tilt of axis and seasonal solar distribution Priority: S - high | Asked: 2017, 2022, 2024 | Marks: 8-20 Year Q. Marks Question focus Tilt of Earth axis and global 2017 1(b) 20 climate variation. Earth-Sun Relationship and global 2022 2(b) 12 climate variation. How tilt affects solar radiation 2024 1(a) 8 distribution and seasons. Earth-Sun geometry: solstices, equinoxes and axial tilt.  Earth axis is about 23.5° from the perpendicular to the orbital plane (equivalent to 66.5° to the orbital plane in the lecture wording).  Because the tilted Earth revolves around the Sun, solar angle and day length change by latitude and season .  Around 21 June the overhead-sun zone reaches the Tropic of Cancer; around 21 December it reaches the Tropic of Capricorn.  Around 21 March and 23 September, solar declination is near the equator (equinox).  Higher sun angle concentrates radiation; lower angle spreads energy over larger area and increases atmospheric path.

title: B1.7 Influence of Topography on climate variation
text: B1.7 Influence of Topography on climate variation Priority: A - repeated | Asked: 2021, 2023, 2024/related | Marks: 5-10 Year Q. Marks Question focus Influence of topography on global 2021 1(a) 10 climate variations. Topographical factors responsible 2023 4(a) 5 for global climate variation. Local site deviations also depend 2024 3(a) related on topography.  Altitude: temperature generally decreases with height; mountain climates differ from valleys .  Slope/aspect: changes solar exposure and therefore surface heating.  Orographic effect: mountains force moist air upward, supporting cloud/rain on windward sides and drier conditions in rain-shadow zones.  Cold-air drainage: dense cool air can settle in depressions/valleys and produce local inversions .  Wind modification: hills, ridges and valleys block, accelerate, channel or create turbulence in airflow . Conclusion Topography does not create the global circulation by itself; it modifies the general climate into distinct regional and site climates.

Tropical climates of maximum 2018 5(c) 10 importance for built-form designers - reasons.  Tropical climates often impose a persistent heat problem, so an unresponsive building accumulates heat for long periods.  Solar control, ventilation and moisture management can be achieved structurally before mechanical systems are sized.  Passive measures operate whenever climate occurs, reducing energy and peak cooling load .  Warm-humid and hot-dry climates need opposite strategies; therefore the built form itself must be climate - specific.  Power reliability, cost and maintenance make passive resilience important in many tropical regions . title: B2.6 Climate-specific protection: Warm-humid measures + Hot-dry
text: B2.6 Climate-specific protection: Warm-humid measures + Hot-dry desert formation, character & precautions Priority: S - high | Asked: 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 | Marks: 10-15 Year Q. Marks Question focus Protective measures in warm- 2021 2(b) 10 humid climate regions. 2022 1(b) 15 Hot-dry desert pattern. Precautions while constructing in 2023 1(c) 10 hot-dry desert climate. How desert forms in subtropical 2024 2(c) 12 region and why day-night range is large. 2021: protective measures in warm-humid climate  Provide maximum ventilation and air movement with large, well-positioned openings.  Provide maximum shading against both direct and diffuse solar radiation.  Avoid unnecessary heat storage; favour light construction where appropriate.  Use reflective/light-coloured outer surfaces and well-insulated, ventilated double roofs .  Use vegetation for shade and microclimate moderation without blocking useful breezes .  Protect walls/openings from heavy rain and moisture while keeping airflow paths open. Hot-dry desert: why it forms and why day-night range is large  Around 20-30° latitude, descending air in the subtropical high suppresses cloud formation and rainfall .  Clear skies allow intense daytime solar heating and strong night-time long-wave radiation .  Low humidity and sparse vegetation mean little latent-heat buffering; surfaces heat and cool rapidly. Hot-dry building precautions  Use compact form and mutual shading to reduce exposed surface area.  Use thick/heavy envelope where useful to exploit thermal mass and time lag.  Keep openings small/controlled during hot dusty periods; use protected night ventilation when outdoor air becomes cooler.  Shade roofs, walls and openings; use light/reflective external surfaces.  Use courtyard and evaporative cooling where water availability permits.  Protect against dust and sand infiltration with screens, vestibules and careful detailing. Source status Warm-humid measures are taken directly from the uploaded design-specification material. Hot-dry protective measures synthesize the tropical-climate characteristics with the uploaded Section A envelope/design principles ; this cross -source synthesis is marked rather than presented as a separate Billah-slide list.

text: B3.4 Temperature inversion Priority: B/A - asked 2018/2021 | Asked: 2018, 2021 | Marks: 10-15 Source status The uploaded question bank names this topic, but the uploaded slides/notes do not contain the full derivation or numerical formula chain. The marked part below uses standard building-physics / solar-geometry knowledge as a supplementary method. Year Q. Marks Question focus Temperature inversion with 2018 6(b) 15 example. Temperature inversion from 2021 3(b) 10 perspective of global warming. The uploaded site-climate slide lists temperature inversion as a deviation factor but does not fully define its mechanism. Standard meteorological meaning: a temperature inversion occurs when temperature increases with height over a layer instead of normally decreasing. Cool dense air can be trapped near the ground beneath warmer air. Typical causes / example  Night-time radiative cooling of ground under clear calm conditions can cool the near-surface air.  Cold air can drain into valleys/depressions and become trapped.  A warm layer above suppresses vertical mixing, allowing fog/smog and pollutants to accumulate . Exam caution Do not claim “global warming causes all inversions”. Treat inversion as a vertical/local atmospheric structure that can intensify urban pollution/thermal discomfort; the question wording “from the perspective of global warming” can be answered by discussing its interaction with urban heat/pollution rather than a direct one-to-one cause.

text: B3.5 Fundamental process of designing a site / residential building using site-climate knowledge Priority: S - repeated | Asked: 2020, 2022, 2023 | Marks: 10 Year Q. Residential building in KUET 2023 3(b) 10 using site-climate knowledge. 14. Collect regional climatic data as the baseline. 15. Identify dominant local modifiers: topography, water, vegetation, existing buildings , soil and windbreaks . 16. Estimate or measure site deviations in temperature, wind, humidity, sun/rain exposure. 17. Observe seasonal extremes and, where long records are unavailable, consult experienced local observers . 18.
