title: B3.6 Urban climate: human intervention, deviation and effects
text: B3.6 Urban climate: human intervention, deviation and effects Priority: S - high | Asked: 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 | Marks: 8-15 Year Q. Marks Question focus 2021 3(a) 10 Urban climate vs macroclimate. Factors and effects of urban- 2022 4(c) 15 climate deviation. Urban climate deviation factors 2023 3(c) 15 and effects. Urban climate depends on human 2024 3(b) 8 intervention - explain. Conceptual urban heat-island profile. Human intervention Urban-climate effect Changed surface qualities - pavement/buildings Higher solar absorption and less evaporation. Building mass and geometry Cast shadows, block/channel wind, store heat and release it slowly. Energy seepage from AC, appliances, engines, industry Adds anthropogenic heat. Reduces outgoing radiation and air quality; can intensify Atmospheric pollution haze/smog. Effects reported in lecture  City-countryside temperature deviation up to about 8°C.  Urban RH about 5-10% lower in the stated slide example due to quick runoff and less vegetation.  Wind velocity may fall to less than half of nearby countryside.  Strong turbulence/eddies can form near leeward building corners.

title: B4.1 Driving Rain and Driving Rain Index (DRI)
text: B4.1 Driving Rain and Driving Rain Index (DRI) Priority: S - highest repeat | Asked: 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 | Marks: 5-10 Year Q. Marks Question focus 2021 3(c-iii) 5 Short note: Driving rain. Driving rain + DRI building 2022 3(c) 10 exposure. 2023 2(c) 10 Driving rain + DRI. Driving rain + building exposure 2024 2(a) 7 by DRI. Driving rain is wind-driven rain that strikes a façade at an angle rather than falling vertically. The oblique impact increases the chance of water penetration at joints, cracks, window reveals and other envelope gaps. DRI = Annual Rainfall (m) × Annual Average Wind Speed (m/s) Lecture unit: m²/s. Driving rain mechanism and exposure classification. Exposure DRI Design response Normal weather detailing; adequate sills, Sheltered < 3 m²/s flashings and joints. More careful reveals, joint sealing, Moderate 3-7 m²/s overhangs and rain screen/drainage. Robust envelope, protected openings, Severe > 7 m²/s drained cavities/rain screen and strong gap control. Slide example: 1.2 m annual rainfall × 4.0 m/s average wind = 4.8 m²/s → Moderate exposure.

title: B4.4 Monthly and Annual Wind Frequency Graph / Wind Rose
text: B4.4 Monthly and Annual Wind Frequency Graph / Wind Rose Priority: A/S - repeated | Asked: 2017, 2024 | Marks: 13-20 Year Q. Marks Question focus Draw monthly and annual wind 2017 3(b) 20 frequency graphs and interpret. Draw monthly and annual wind 2024 4(a) 13 frequency graph and explain interpretation. Wind rose: direction, frequency, speed classes and calm percentage.  Each spoke points toward the direction FROM which wind arrives.  Spoke length represents frequency of occurrence from that direction.  Segment/line thickness or colour can represent speed classes.  Calm percentage may be shown at the centre.  A monthly graph shows seasonal change; the annual graph aggregates the whole year and identifies the dominant prevailing directions. Design interpretation  Orient openings and building spacing to desirable seasonal winds .  Protect façades from harmful hot/dusty/cold winds.  Locate service/buffer zones on adverse wind sides.  Combine wind-frequency data with driving-rain exposure before locating openings .

Precipitation / driving rain Roof pitch, drainage, joints, waterproofing and protected openings. Solar radiation Orientation, shading, glazing, roof/wall heat gain and daylight. Ventilation, infiltration, pressure, structural exposure and rain Wind penetration. Sky condition Diffuse radiation/daylight and solar availability. title: B4.6 Humidity factors and reciprocal climate relationships
text: B4.6 Humidity factors and reciprocal climate relationships Priority: B/A - one direct paper | Asked: 2020 | Marks: 15 Year Q. Marks Question focus Humidity depends on soil, waterbody, altitude, precipitation, 2020 1(b) 15 air movement and vegetation; show reciprocal relationship. Factor Effect on humidity / related climate Wet/vegetated soil supports evaporation; dry/stony surfaces tend Soil condition to contribute less local moisture. Evaporation increases atmospheric moisture and moderates Water body temperature. Temperature falls with height; cooling can raise RH and support Altitude condensation/cloud. Adds surface moisture and wetness; subsequent evaporation can Precipitation raise humidity. Air movement Transports moist/dry air and controls evaporation rate. Evapotranspiration adds moisture; shade lowers surface Vegetation temperature and modifies local RH. The relationships are reciprocal: humidity changes evaporation, cloud and precipitation ; those processes in turn modify radiation, temperature and airflow, so the climatic elements interact rather than operate independently .

title: B4.7 Atmospheric Pressure
text: B4.7 Atmospheric Pressure Priority: B - short repeated | Asked: 2022, 2023 | Marks: 5 Year Q. Marks Question focus Briefly describe atmospheric 2022 3(a) 5 pressure. Briefly describe atmospheric 2023 2(d) 5 pressure. Atmospheric pressure is the force per unit area exerted by the weight of the air column above a surface . In moist air it can be considered as the sum of the partial pressure of dry air and the partial pressure of water vapour . P = P_a + P_v P_a = partial pressure of dry air; P_v = vapour pressure.  Pressure generally decreases with altitude.  Pressure differences drive wind from higher toward lower pressure, then Coriolis and friction modify direction .  Heating can make air less dense and contribute to rising motion/low-pressure development.

title: B4.8 Solar radiation quantity / duration vs intensity
text: B4.8 Solar radiation quantity / duration vs intensity Priority: B/A - short support | Asked: 2021, 2024/related | Marks: 5 Year Q. Marks Question focus Short note: Solar radiation 2021 3(c-i) 5 quantity. 2024 4(c) related Radiation at Earth surface. The course slide gives a solar constant of about 1395 W/m² at the upper atmosphere and notes variations from solar output and Earth-Sun distance. At a building site, distinguish sunshine duration from radiation intensity : duration tells how long bright sun occurs; intensity is actual radiant power per unit area . Quantity Typical unit / instrument Sunshine duration hours/day; Campbell-Stokes sunshine recorder. Radiation intensity W/m²; pyranometer/pyrheliometer/actinometer/solarimeter.

Exam-ready minimum from Lecture 01
• Climate: given / long-term environmental condition - especially temperature, humidity, precipitation, wind and solar radiation.
• Context: landform, geography and the physical/cultural setting within which the building must fit.
• Comfort: desirable occupant condition - thermal, visual, acoustic and air-quality satisfaction.
• Man-made environment: human modification of the environment to obtain shelter and comfort.
• Mitigation position: neither accept environmental stress passively nor reject development; design with the environment to reduce impact.
• Climatic control framework: mechanical control, structural control and ventilation system.
• High-return answer structure: Definition -> key factors -> design consideration -> one practical example -> conclusion.
Final
recommendation
If time is short, memorize Slides 19-20 first. They answer the most repeated direct cluster. Then study Slides 16-18 for the mitigation / design-with-environment
argument. Treat responsibility, passive-active control, thermal comfort, site climate and climate-friendly construction as bridge topics only in Lecture 01 and
move to their dedicated lectures for full answers.
